title: Mug Scrambled Eggs
instructions:
Butter a large mug — use one at least twice the volume of the egg, because the mixture climbs as it sets. Crack the eggs into the mug and beat them thoroughly with a fork until no streaks of white remain; never microwave an egg in its shell, and never leave a yolk whole, as an intact yolk can burst after you take it out. Beat in the milk and salt.

Microwave on high for 30 seconds, then stir with the fork, scraping the cooked edges into the centre. Continue in 15-second bursts, stirring after each, until the eggs are just set and no longer glossy — about 1 to 1 1/2 minutes total in a 1000W oven. They should reach 160°F.

Let the mug stand for 1 minute before eating. The eggs finish cooking in that minute and the mug will be hotter than you expect.

title: Porridge in a Bowl
instructions:
Combine the oats, milk and salt in a deep bowl. Use a bowl at least three times as deep as the liquid — milk foams up fast and boiling over is the usual way this goes wrong.

Microwave on high for 2 minutes, then stir. Continue in 30-second bursts, stirring after each, until the oats are thick and creamy — about 3 minutes total in a 1000W oven. If it threatens to climb the bowl, stop the oven, stir, and carry on at half power.

Stir in the honey and let it stand for 1 minute to thicken before eating.

title: Microwave Baked Potato
instructions:
Scrub the potato and pat it dry. Pierce it right through in six or eight places with a fork — an unpierced potato traps steam and can burst. Do not skip this.

Set it on a plate and microwave on high for 5 minutes. Turn it over and give it another 3 to 5 minutes, until a knife slides into the centre with no resistance. Timing depends on size more than anything else, so test rather than trust the clock.

Let it stand for 2 minutes — the centre keeps cooking. Split it open, taking care with the steam, and work in the butter, salt and pepper.

title: Steamed Broccoli
instructions:
Cut the broccoli into florets of roughly equal size — uneven pieces cook unevenly, and the microwave will not correct for it. Put them in a bowl with the water.

Cover the bowl with a plate, leaving a gap at one side for steam to escape. Microwave on high for 3 minutes, then check: the florets should be bright green and just tender at the stem. Give them another minute if they are still firm.

Uncover away from your face — the trapped steam is the burn risk here, not the bowl. Drain, then toss with the olive oil and salt.

title: Mug Mac and Cheese
instructions:
Put the macaroni, water and salt in a large mug — again, at least twice the volume you think you need, because the water foams.

Microwave on high for 2 minutes, then stir. Repeat in 2-minute bursts, stirring each time, until the pasta is tender and most of the water is gone, about 6 to 8 minutes in a 1000W oven. Add a splash more water if it dries out before the pasta softens.

Stir in the milk and the grated cheddar. Microwave for a final 30 seconds, then stir hard until the sauce comes together and coats the pasta. Let it stand a minute before eating.

title: Poached Cod with Lemon
instructions:
Put the fillet in a shallow dish, tucking the thin tail end under itself so the piece is an even thickness — this is what stops the thin end overcooking before the middle is done. Spoon over the lemon juice and olive oil, and season.

Cover the dish with a plate, leaving a gap for steam. Microwave on high for 2 minutes, then check. Continue in 30-second bursts until the flesh is opaque all the way through and flakes cleanly when you press it with a fork — usually 3 to 4 minutes total for a 150g fillet. Cod should reach 145°F.

Let it stand, still covered, for 3 minutes before serving. The standing time is part of the cooking, not a pause after it.

title: Rice and Peas Bowl
instructions:
Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then put it in a deep bowl with the water and salt. The bowl needs plenty of headroom — rice water boils over readily.

Microwave uncovered on high for 5 minutes, then reduce to medium power and cook for another 6 to 8 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

Stir in the frozen peas, cover with a plate, and microwave for 1 minute more. Let it stand covered for 3 minutes, then fluff with a fork. The rice finishes steaming in that time and will be gluey if you skip it.

title: Garlic Green Beans
instructions:
Trim the beans and lay them in a shallow dish in as close to a single layer as you can manage — piled beans steam unevenly. Add the water.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap, and microwave on high for 3 minutes. Shake the dish and check: the beans should be bright green and tender with some bite left. Give them another minute if needed.

Drain off the water. Add the olive oil, sliced garlic and salt, toss well, and microwave uncovered for 45 seconds more — just enough to take the raw edge off the garlic without browning it.

title: Cheesy Egg Mug
instructions:
Crack the eggs into a large mug and beat them thoroughly with a fork until the yolks and whites are fully combined — never cook an egg in its shell, and never leave a yolk intact, because a whole yolk can burst after heating. Beat in the milk, salt and pepper.

Microwave on high for 30 seconds, stir, then continue in 15-second bursts, stirring each time, until the eggs are just set — around 1 1/2 minutes in a 1000W oven, to 160°F.

Stir in the grated cheddar while the eggs are still hot and let the mug stand for 1 minute. The residual heat melts the cheese and finishes the eggs.

title: Black Bean and Sweetcorn Bowl
instructions:
Drain and rinse the beans and sweetcorn well — the canning liquid will make the finished bowl taste flat and metallic. Tip both into a bowl and stir through the cumin, olive oil and salt.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap for steam, and microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir, then give it another minute until heated right through and steaming in the centre, not just at the edges.

Stir once more and let it stand for 1 minute. Both ingredients are already cooked, so you are only heating them — going longer will burst the beans.

title: Banana Cinnamon Oats
instructions:
Put the oats and milk in a deep bowl — deep enough that the milk fills less than a third of it, because it foams up sharply as it boils.

Microwave on high for 2 minutes, then stir. Continue in 30-second bursts, stirring after each, until thick and creamy, about 3 minutes in total.

Stir in the cinnamon and half the sliced banana, letting it soften into the oats. Top with the rest and let the bowl stand for 1 minute before eating.

title: Honey Glazed Carrots
instructions:
Slice the carrots into rounds of even thickness, about 5mm. Evenness matters more here than in most recipes, because a thick round and a thin one will not finish together. Put them in a bowl with the water.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap, and microwave on high for 4 minutes. Stir, then continue for 2 to 3 minutes more until tender when pierced.

Drain, then add the butter, honey and salt and microwave uncovered for 45 seconds. Stir well so the glaze coats the carrots and let stand for a minute.

title: Herbed Couscous
instructions:
Put the water and crumbled stock cube in a bowl and microwave on high for 2 minutes, until steaming and the cube has dissolved.

Stir in the couscous and the olive oil, cover with a plate, and leave it to stand off the heat for 5 minutes. Couscous is not really cooked so much as hydrated — the microwave's job is to get the liquid hot, and the standing time does the rest. Microwaving it further will turn it to paste.

Fluff thoroughly with a fork, breaking up any clumps, and stir through the chopped parsley.

title: Wilted Spinach with Garlic and Lemon
instructions:
Wash the spinach and leave it wet — the water clinging to the leaves is all the liquid it needs. Pile it into a large bowl; it will look like far too much and will collapse to a quarter of the volume.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap, and microwave on high for 1 1/2 minutes. Stir to bring the uncooked leaves from the top down to the bottom, then give it another 30 to 60 seconds until everything is just wilted.

Tip out the liquid that has collected, then toss the spinach with the olive oil, sliced garlic, lemon juice and salt. Serve straight away — it turns dull and watery if it sits.

title: Lemon Salmon Fillet
instructions:
Set the fillet skin-side down in a shallow dish. Rub it with the olive oil, season, and lay the lemon slices over the top. If one end is noticeably thinner, fold it under so the fillet cooks at one rate.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap for steam, and microwave on medium power rather than high — salmon toughens and weeps white protein if driven too hard. Give it 3 minutes, then check every 30 seconds until the flesh is opaque and flakes under gentle pressure, about 4 minutes total for 150g. Salmon should reach 145°F.

Leave it covered for 3 minutes before serving. It carries on cooking as it stands.

title: Spiced Lentil Bowl
instructions:
Rinse the red lentils until the water runs clear. Put them in a deep bowl with the water and the crumbled stock cube — use a bowl with real headroom, as lentils froth heavily.

Microwave on high for 4 minutes, watching it, then stir and drop to medium power. Continue for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick purée. Add a splash of water if it tightens up before they soften.

Stir in the cumin and salt and let it stand for 2 minutes. Use red lentils rather than green or brown — they break down without soaking, which the others will not do in this time.

title: Microwave Quinoa
instructions:
Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve for a good 30 seconds. The seeds carry a natural coating that tastes bitter and soapy if it is left on, and rinsing is the only way to remove it.

Put it in a deep bowl with the water and salt. Microwave uncovered on high for 4 minutes, then reduce to medium and cook for 8 minutes more, until the water is absorbed and you can see the little spiral germ separating from each seed.

Cover and let it stand for 3 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir through the olive oil.

title: Buttered Garlic Mushrooms
instructions:
Wipe the mushrooms clean rather than washing them, and slice them evenly. Put them in a bowl with the butter and minced garlic. Do not add any water — mushrooms release a surprising amount of their own.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap, and microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir, then continue for 2 to 3 minutes more until they have shrunk, darkened, and are sitting in their own buttery liquid.

Season with salt at the end rather than the start; salting early draws the water out too fast and leaves them rubbery. Stir through the parsley and let stand for a minute.

title: Peanut Butter Oats
instructions:
Combine the oats and milk in a deep bowl, filling it no more than a third full — the milk foams up hard as it comes to the boil.

Microwave on high for 2 minutes, stir, then continue in 30-second bursts until thick and creamy, about 3 minutes total.

Stir in the peanut butter straight away while the oats are hot, working it through until it melts into the porridge rather than sitting in a lump. Drizzle with honey and let it stand for a minute.

title: Warm Chickpea and Tomato Bowl
instructions:
Drain and rinse the chickpeas well. Chop the tomatoes and put both in a bowl with the olive oil, cumin and salt, stirring so the spice coats everything rather than sitting on top.

Cover with a plate, leaving a gap for steam, and microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir, then give it another 1 to 2 minutes until the tomatoes have slumped and released their juice and the chickpeas are hot through.

Stir well and let it stand for 1 minute. Crush a few of the chickpeas against the side of the bowl with a fork if you want the juices to thicken.

title: Microwave Personal Pizza
instructions:
Set the pita on a microwave-safe plate and spread the tomato sauce almost to the edge, leaving a narrow rim so it does not run off. Scatter the mozzarella, sweetcorn and oregano evenly over the top. Use cooked or ready-to-eat toppings only; the microwave melts and heats toppings but is not a reliable way to cook raw meat.

Microwave on high for 60 to 90 seconds, checking after 60 seconds, until the cheese is fully melted and the centre is steaming. Microwave ovens vary, so add 15-second bursts rather than letting the cheese dry out.

Let the pizza stand for 1 minute before eating. The plate and cheese stay hot after the oven stops, and the short rest lets the topping set enough to slice safely.

title: Microwave Bean & Cheese Burrito
instructions:
Warm the tortilla under a slightly damp paper towel for 15 seconds so it rolls without splitting. Spread the refried beans in a strip across the lower third, keeping the edges clear, then add the cheddar and salsa. Fold the bottom up, fold in both sides, and roll firmly into a burrito with the seam underneath.

Place it seam-side down on a microwave-safe plate and cover with a damp paper towel. Microwave on high for 60 to 90 seconds, turning once, until the beans are steaming hot and the cheese has melted. Add 15-second bursts if the centre is not hot.

Let it stand covered for 1 minute before unwrapping. Steam escapes when the towel is lifted, so open it away from your face and check the centre before eating.

title: Microwave Breakfast Burrito
instructions:
Beat the egg and milk thoroughly with a fork in a large microwave-safe mug until the yolk and white are completely combined. This prevents an intact yolk from bursting as it heats. Microwave on high for 30 seconds, stir and scrape the sides, then continue in 15-second bursts until the egg is set but still moist, about 60 to 90 seconds total; it should reach 160°F.

Warm the tortilla under a damp paper towel for 15 seconds. Tip the scrambled egg into the centre, add the cheddar and salsa, fold in the sides and roll into a burrito. Return it seam-side down to the plate and microwave for 20 to 30 seconds, until the cheese softens.

Let the burrito stand for 1 minute before eating. Check that the centre is hot and open it carefully because steam collects inside the fold.

title: Microwave Cheese Quesadilla
instructions:
Lay the tortilla flat on a microwave-safe plate and scatter the cheddar over one half, leaving a small border so melted cheese does not run over the edge. Fold the bare half over the cheese and press gently so the fold stays closed. Use only ready-to-eat fillings in this microwave version; it is designed to melt cheese and warm the tortilla, not cook raw meat.

Microwave on high for 45 seconds, then check the cheese. Continue in 15-second bursts until the cheese is melted and the tortilla is warm, usually 60 to 90 seconds total. Letting the tortilla heat gradually keeps it flexible instead of tough.

Let it stand for 1 minute, then cut into wedges and serve with the salsa. The melted cheese remains very hot after heating, so test a small corner before taking a full bite.

title: Microwave Mug Mac & Cheese
instructions:
Put the macaroni and water in a very large microwave-safe mug or bowl; leave at least half the vessel empty because pasta water foams. Microwave on high for 2 minutes, stir carefully, and repeat in 1-minute bursts until the pasta is tender and most of the water has been absorbed, about 5 to 6 minutes total. Add a tablespoon of water if the pasta is still firm but the mug is dry.

Stir in the milk, butter and shredded cheddar while the pasta is hot. Microwave for 30 seconds, stir until smooth, and add another 15 seconds only if the cheese has not melted. The mixture will thicken as it cools.

Let the mug stand for 1 minute before eating. Stir once more, check the centre is hot, and handle the mug with a cloth because both the vessel and sauce retain heat.

title: Microwave Loaded Baked Potato
instructions:
Scrub the potato and pat it dry. Pierce it deeply in six to eight places with a fork so steam can escape; an unpierced potato can burst. Put it on a microwave-safe plate and microwave on high for 4 minutes. Turn it over and continue for 2 to 3 minutes, until a knife slides into the centre easily.

Let the potato stand for 2 minutes before opening it. The centre continues cooking during this rest and the steam pressure settles. Split it carefully, fluff the flesh with a fork, and work in the butter, salt and black pepper.

Top with the cheddar and microwave for 30 to 45 seconds, until the cheese melts. Let it stand for another 30 seconds, then check the centre and serve; the potato and filling will be extremely hot immediately after heating.

title: Microwave Steamed Rice & Veggie Bowl
instructions:
Put the cooked or instant rice and frozen mixed vegetables in a large microwave-safe bowl. Break up any compacted rice and cover the bowl with a vented microwave lid or a plate left slightly ajar so steam can escape. Microwave on high for 2 minutes, stir from the edges into the centre, then heat for 1 to 2 minutes more until the vegetables are tender and the rice is steaming throughout.

Stir in the soy sauce and sesame seed oil. If the centre is not hot, return the bowl for another 30 seconds; reheating in short bursts prevents the rice from drying out. Use rice that was refrigerated promptly and reheat it only once.

Let the bowl stand covered for 1 minute so the heat evens out, then uncover away from your face and stir again before eating. The bowl, steam and sauce will all be hot.

title: Peanut Butter and Jelly Sandwich
instructions: Spread peanut butter evenly over one slice of bread and jam over the other slice. Press the slices together and cut in half if desired.

title: Classic Grilled Cheese
instructions: Butter one side of each bread slice. Place one slice butter-side down in a skillet over medium heat, layer with cheddar cheese, and top with the second bread slice butter-side up. Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden, flip, and cook until cheese is melted.

title: Toast with Butter and Jam
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden brown. Spread butter evenly while warm, then spread jam over top.

title: Classic Scrambled Eggs
instructions: Whisk eggs with salt and black pepper in a bowl. Melt butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour in the eggs and gently stir with a spatula until soft curds form and eggs are just set (about 2-3 minutes). Remove from heat immediately.

title: Simple Tuna Salad Sandwich
instructions: Drain tuna and mix with mayonnaise, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Spread tuna salad between two slices of bread, slice in half, and serve.

title: Cinnamon Sugar Toast
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden brown. Spread butter over warm toast, then sprinkle evenly with mixed sugar and cinnamon.
